Definition: to smell bad; figuratively, to be offensive morally
BiblicalUsage: Ba'ash means to stink, to smell bad — and in Scripture a bad smell is a bad reputation. The Philistines made Israel abhorred, the men of Jabesh made themselves odious to the Ammonites, the dead fish of Egypt stank in the river, and the Preacher says dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour. A small offence spoils a sweet thing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a reputation is like ointment: one dead fly can spoil the whole pot. The wise man keeps the flies out.
